The **67th Academy Awards** ceremony, organized by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") (AMPAS) took place on March 27, 1995, at the [Shrine Auditorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_Auditorium "Shrine Auditorium") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") beginning at 6:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 9:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"). During the ceremony, AMPAS presented Academy Awards (commonly referred to as the Oscars) in 23 categories honoring the [films released in 1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_in_film "1994 in film"). The ceremony, televised in the United States by [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company"), was produced by [Gilbert Cates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Cates "Gilbert Cates") and directed by [Jeff Margolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Margolis "Jeff Margolis").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-3) Comedian [David Letterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Letterman "David Letterman") hosted the show for the first time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-4) Three weeks earlier in a ceremony held at the [Regent Beverly Wilshire Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Wilshire_Hotel "Beverly Wilshire Hotel") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California") on March 4, the [Academy Awards for Technical Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Technical_Achievement "Academy Award for Technical Achievement") were presented by host [Jamie Lee Curtis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Lee_Curtis "Jamie Lee Curtis").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-5)

_[Forrest Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forrest\_Gump "Forrest Gump")_ won six awards, including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-6) Other winners included _[Ed Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed\_Wood\_(film) "Ed Wood (film)")_, _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King "The Lion King")_, and _[Speed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speed\_(1994\_film) "Speed (1994 film)")_ with two awards and _[The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Priscilla,\_Queen\_of\_the\_Desert "The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert")_; _[Blue Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Sky\_(1994\_film) "Blue Sky (1994 film)")_, _[Bob's Birthday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob's\_Birthday "Bob's Birthday")_, _[Bullets Over Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullets\_Over\_Broadway "Bullets Over Broadway")_, _[Burnt by the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnt\_by\_the\_Sun "Burnt by the Sun")_, _[Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz\_Kafka's\_It's\_a\_Wonderful\_Life "Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life")_, _[Legends of the Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legends\_of\_the\_Fall "Legends of the Fall")_, _[The Madness of King George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Madness\_of\_King\_George "The Madness of King George")_, _[Maya Lin: A Strong Clear Vision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maya\_Lin:\_A\_Strong\_Clear\_Vision "Maya Lin: A Strong Clear Vision")_, _[Pulp Fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulp\_Fiction "Pulp Fiction")_, _[A Time for Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Time\_for\_Justice "A Time for Justice")_, and _[Trevor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor\_(film) "Trevor (film)")_ with one. The telecast garnered more than 48 million viewers in the United States, making it the most watched Oscars telecast since the [55th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55th_Academy_Awards "55th Academy Awards") in 1983.

## Winners and nominees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Winners and nominees")]

The nominees for the 67th Academy Awards were announced on February 14, 1995, at the [Samuel Goldwyn Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Goldwyn_Theater "Samuel Goldwyn Theater") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), by [Arthur Hiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Hiller "Arthur Hiller"), the then-president of the Academy, and actress [Angela Bassett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Bassett "Angela Bassett").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-7)_[Forrest Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forrest\_Gump "Forrest Gump")_ earned the most nominations with thirteen. It was the most nominated film since 1966's _[Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who's\_Afraid\_of\_Virginia\_Woolf%3F\_(film) "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (film)")_ and the fifth film to earn that many nominations.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-8)_[Bullets Over Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullets\_Over\_Broadway "Bullets Over Broadway")_, _[Pulp Fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulp\_Fiction "Pulp Fiction")_, and _[The Shawshank Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shawshank\_Redemption "The Shawshank Redemption")_ tied for second with seven each.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-9)

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 27, 1995. _Forrest Gump_ was the highest grossing [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture") winner in history.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-LAT-10) For only the second time in Oscar history, three of the four acting winners were previous winners. The [11th ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/11th_Academy_Awards "11th Academy Awards") held in 1939 previously accomplished this feat.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-11) Best Actor winner [Tom Hanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hanks "Tom Hanks") became the fifth performer to win consecutive acting Oscars and the second person to do so in the aforementioned category since [Spencer Tracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spencer_Tracy "Spencer Tracy") won for his performances in _[Captains Courageous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captains\_Courageous\_(1937\_film) "Captains Courageous (1937 film)")_ (1937) and _[Boys Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boys\_Town\_(film) "Boys Town (film)")_ (1938).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-12)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-LAT-10) He also was the sixth person to win Best Actor twice.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-13) Best Supporting Actress winner [Dianne Wiest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dianne_Wiest "Dianne Wiest") became the first person to win two acting Oscars for performances in films directed by the same person.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-14) She first won in that same category for her role in [Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen")'s 1986 film _[Hannah and Her Sisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah\_and\_Her\_Sisters "Hannah and Her Sisters")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-15)_[Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz\_Kafka's\_It's\_a\_Wonderful\_Life "Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life")_ and _[Trevor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor\_(film) "Trevor (film)")_'s joint win in the Best Live Action Short category marked the fifth occurrence of a tie in Oscar history; the next tie would occur at the [85th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/85th_Academy_Awards "85th Academy Awards") in 2013.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-16)

## Ceremony information

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Ceremony information")]

Despite earning critical praise for the [previous year's ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards "66th Academy Awards"), actress and comedian [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") announced that she would not host the ceremony for a second consecutive year saying, "I've had a great time, but I've done it."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-22) She added that her role in the upcoming movie _[Bogus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogus\_(film) "Bogus (film)")_ would jeopardize her busy schedule.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-No_Goldberg_or_Crystal-23) In addition, her [Comic Relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_Relief_USA "Comic Relief USA") co-host and veteran Oscar emcee [Billy Crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Crystal "Billy Crystal") declined to host the show citing his commitment to his film _[Forget Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forget\_Paris "Forget Paris")_ which he directed, wrote, starred in, and produced.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-No_Goldberg_or_Crystal-23) Producer Gil Cates hired actor, comedian, and _[Late Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Show\_with\_David\_Letterman "Late Show with David Letterman")_ host [David Letterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Letterman "David Letterman") as host of the 1995 ceremony.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-24) Cates explained his decision to hire the late-night talk show host saying, "He's punctual, he's well groomed, and he knows how to keep an audience awake."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Comedy-25)[ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") entertainment president [Ted Harbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Harbert "Ted Harbert") also approved of the choice stating, "If Dave likes the experience, this could be a great answer for the show, just the way [Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Carson "Johnny Carson") did the show for many years."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-26)

As with previous ceremonies he produced, Cates centered the show on a theme. This year, he christened the show with the theme "Comedy and the Movies" commenting "This year, because of the earthquakes and floods and [Bosnia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia "Bosnia") and [Rwanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwanda "Rwanda"), it was a (terrible) year, and therefore seemed a great year to celebrate what movies can really give us, which is an opportunity to go for two hours in the dark and laugh together. Even with television, it's not a community experience unless you have a very big family. So it's unique to movies and theater, and it's this very human thing."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Comedy-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Comedy_Oscars-27) In tandem with the theme, the ceremony's opening number featured a montage produced by [Chuck Workman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Workman "Chuck Workman") featuring scenes of humorous moments from a variety of both comedic and non-comedic films projected on a large screen on the stage. During that segment, actors [Tim Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Curry "Tim Curry"), [Kathy Najimy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Najimy "Kathy Najimy"), and [Mara Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mara_Wilson "Mara Wilson") performed a modified version of the song "[Make 'Em Laugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Make_'Em_Laugh "Make 'Em Laugh")" from the film _[Singin' in the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singin'\_in\_the\_Rain "Singin' in the Rain")_, using [blue screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chroma_key "Chroma key") technology to make it appear that they were jumping in and out of the montage on the screen.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-28) Several collections of film clips were shown throughout the broadcast highlighting various aspects of comedy such as troupes and dialogue.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-29)

Several other people were also involved with the production of the ceremony. [Bill Conti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Conti "Bill Conti") served as musical director and conductor for the event.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-30) Production designer Roy Christopher designed a new stage for the ceremony which prominently featured a [proscenium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proscenium "Proscenium") which was designed to resemble the iris of a camera.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-31) Moreover, Christopher commented that the iris motif was inspired by the [iris shot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_shot "Iris shot") prominently featured in several comedic films and shorts.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Comedy_Oscars-27) Dancer Debbie Allen choreographed _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King "The Lion King")_ musical number.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-32) Actors [Alec Baldwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alec_Baldwin "Alec Baldwin"), [Jack Lemmon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Lemmon "Jack Lemmon"), [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin"), and [Rosie O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosie_O'Donnell "Rosie O'Donnell") participated in a pre-taped comedic sketch lampooning auditions for a role in _[Cabin Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabin\_Boy "Cabin Boy")_, the film in which Letterman made his film acting debut.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Wiley_1996_982-33)

### Box office performance of nominees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Box office performance of nominees")]

At the time of the nominations announcement on February 14, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees at the US box office was $468 million, with an average of $93.6 million per film.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-BoxOfficeOscars-34)_Forrest Gump_ was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees with $300 million in domestic box office receipts. The film was followed by _Pulp Fiction_ ($76 million), _Four Weddings and a Funeral_ ($52 million), _Quiz Show_ ($21 million) and _The Shawshank Redemption_ ($16 million).[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-BoxOfficeOscars-34)

Of the top 50 grossing movies of the year, 44 nominations went to 14 films on the list. Only _Forrest Gump_ (2nd), _The Client_ (12th), _Pulp Fiction_ (14th), _Four Weddings and a Funeral_ (20th), and _Nell_ (41st) were nominated for directing, acting, screenwriting, or Best Picture. The other top 50 box office hits that earned nominations were _The Lion King_ (1st), _True Lies_ (3rd), _Clear and Present Danger_ (6th), _Speed_ (7th), _The Mask_ (8th), _Interview with the Vampire_ (10th), _Maverick_ (11th), _Legends of the Fall_ (27th) and _Little Women_ (31st).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-35)

### Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

The show received a negative reception from most media publications. John J. O'Connor of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ wrote, "Instead of keeping things moving smartly, Mr. Letterman stuck with his late-night shtick, too often leaving the show's pacing in shambles." He also added, "Within the show's first half-hour, with no strong hand at the helm, the audience simply sagged. Applause died long before most winners even reached the podium."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-36) Television critic John Carman of the _[San Francisco Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Francisco\_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle")_ commented, "Last night on ABC, no one got it. Hollywood's big event was wonderfully littered by technical errors, bad taste, low comedy and lower necklines." Moreover, he remarked, "Letterman, the rookie host, was off his game in his opening monologue. Maybe it was the big auditorium. Or a billion people in the television audience."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-37) Film critic [Andrew Sarris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Sarris "Andrew Sarris") of _[The New York Observer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Observer "The New York Observer")_ quipped, "Not only was he not witty or funny, he never knew when to let bad enough alone." He concluded, "As the evening dragged on, it became obvious that Mr. Letterman had no gift for ad-libbing through the few unpredictable opportunities in a 'live' event like the Oscars."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-38)

Some media outlets received the broadcast more positively. Television critic Joyce Millman of _[The San Francisco Examiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_San\_Francisco\_Examiner "The San Francisco Examiner")_ noted, "In his first stint as host of the Oscar telecast, David Letterman did the impossible—he made something entertaining from what is traditionally the most boring three hours of TV this side of a [test pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testcard "Testcard")."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-39)_[The Buffalo News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Buffalo\_News "The Buffalo News")_ columnist Alan Pergament praised Letterman's performance as host writing "David Letterman was a box full of chocolates on an Oscar night that was empty of much emotion until the expected _Forrest Gump_ sweep in the final 15 minutes." He also added that despite a lack of surprises amongst the awards, the emotional and unexpected humorous moments provided depth and entertainment throughout the evening.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-40) Hal Boedeker of the _[Orlando Sentinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando\_Sentinel "Orlando Sentinel")_ gave an average review of the ceremony but singled out Letterman noting that he "proved Monday night that he's among Oscar's Top 10 Hosts. He's definitely at the top of the list with Johnny Carson, Billy Crystal and [Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope "Bob Hope")."[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-41)

### Ratings and reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Ratings and reception")]

The American telecast on ABC drew an average of 48.28 million people over its length, which was a 7% increase from the [previous year's ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards "66th Academy Awards").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Oscar_ratings-42)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-LA-43) An estimated 81 million total viewers watched all or part of the awards.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-44) The show also drew higher [Nielsen ratings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_ratings "Nielsen ratings") compared to the previous ceremony with 32.5% of households watching over a 53 share.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-LA-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-TVB_Oscars-45) It also drew a higher 18–49 demographic rating with a 21.7 rating among viewers in that demographic.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-TVB_Oscars-45) It was the most watched Oscars telecast since the [55th ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55th_Academy_Awards "55th Academy Awards") held in 1983.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-46)

In July 1995, the ceremony presentation received six nominations at the [47th Primetime Emmys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/47th_Primetime_Emmy_Awards "47th Primetime Emmy Awards").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-47) Two months later, the ceremony won one of those nominations for Jeff Margolis's direction of the telecast.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-48)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-49)

The **67th Academy Awards** ceremony, organized by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") (AMPAS) took place on March 27, 1995, at the [Shrine Auditorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrine_Auditorium "Shrine Auditorium") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") beginning at 6:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 9:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"). During the ceremony, AMPAS presented Academy Awards (commonly referred to as the Oscars) in 23 categories honoring the [films released in 1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_in_film "1994 in film"). The ceremony, televised in the United States by [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company"), was produced by [Gilbert Cates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Cates "Gilbert Cates") and directed by [Jeff Margolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Margolis "Jeff Margolis").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-3) Comedian [David Letterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Letterman "David Letterman") hosted the show for the first time.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-4) Three weeks earlier in a ceremony held at the [Regent Beverly Wilshire Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Wilshire_Hotel "Beverly Wilshire Hotel") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California") on March 4, the [Academy Awards for Technical Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Technical_Achievement "Academy Award for Technical Achievement") were presented by host [Jamie Lee Curtis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Lee_Curtis "Jamie Lee Curtis").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-5)

_[Forrest Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forrest\_Gump "Forrest Gump")_ won six awards, including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-6) Other winners included _[Ed Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed\_Wood\_(film) "Ed Wood (film)")_, _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King "The Lion King")_, and _[Speed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speed\_(1994\_film) "Speed (1994 film)")_ with two awards and _[The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Priscilla,\_Queen\_of\_the\_Desert "The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert")_; _[Blue Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Sky\_(1994\_film) "Blue Sky (1994 film)")_, _[Bob's Birthday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob's\_Birthday "Bob's Birthday")_, _[Bullets Over Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullets\_Over\_Broadway "Bullets Over Broadway")_, _[Burnt by the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnt\_by\_the\_Sun "Burnt by the Sun")_, _[Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz\_Kafka's\_It's\_a\_Wonderful\_Life "Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life")_, _[Legends of the Fall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legends\_of\_the\_Fall "Legends of the Fall")_, _[The Madness of King George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Madness\_of\_King\_George "The Madness of King George")_, _[Maya Lin: A Strong Clear Vision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maya\_Lin:\_A\_Strong\_Clear\_Vision "Maya Lin: A Strong Clear Vision")_, _[Pulp Fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulp\_Fiction "Pulp Fiction")_, _[A Time for Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Time\_for\_Justice "A Time for Justice")_, and _[Trevor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor\_(film) "Trevor (film)")_ with one. The telecast garnered more than 48 million viewers in the United States, making it the most watched Oscars telecast since the [55th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55th_Academy_Awards "55th Academy Awards") in 1983.

## Winners and nominees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Winners and nominees")]

The nominees for the 67th Academy Awards were announced on February 14, 1995, at the [Samuel Goldwyn Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Goldwyn_Theater "Samuel Goldwyn Theater") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), by [Arthur Hiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Hiller "Arthur Hiller"), the then-president of the Academy, and actress [Angela Bassett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Bassett "Angela Bassett").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-7)_[Forrest Gump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forrest\_Gump "Forrest Gump")_ earned the most nominations with thirteen. It was the most nominated film since 1966's _[Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who's\_Afraid\_of\_Virginia\_Woolf%3F\_(film) "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (film)")_ and the fifth film to earn that many nominations.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-8)_[Bullets Over Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullets\_Over\_Broadway "Bullets Over Broadway")_, _[Pulp Fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulp\_Fiction "Pulp Fiction")_, and _[The Shawshank Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shawshank\_Redemption "The Shawshank Redemption")_ tied for second with seven each.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-9)

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 27, 1995. _Forrest Gump_ was the highest grossing [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture") winner in history.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-LAT-10) For only the second time in Oscar history, three of the four acting winners were previous winners. The [11th ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/11th_Academy_Awards "11th Academy Awards") held in 1939 previously accomplished this feat.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-11) Best Actor winner [Tom Hanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hanks "Tom Hanks") became the fifth performer to win consecutive acting Oscars and the second person to do so in the aforementioned category since [Spencer Tracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spencer_Tracy "Spencer Tracy") won for his performances in _[Captains Courageous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captains\_Courageous\_(1937\_film) "Captains Courageous (1937 film)")_ (1937) and _[Boys Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boys\_Town\_(film) "Boys Town (film)")_ (1938).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-12)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-LAT-10) He also was the sixth person to win Best Actor twice.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-13) Best Supporting Actress winner [Dianne Wiest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dianne_Wiest "Dianne Wiest") became the first person to win two acting Oscars for performances in films directed by the same person.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-14) She first won in that same category for her role in [Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen")'s 1986 film _[Hannah and Her Sisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah\_and\_Her\_Sisters "Hannah and Her Sisters")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-15)_[Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz\_Kafka's\_It's\_a\_Wonderful\_Life "Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life")_ and _[Trevor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor\_(film) "Trevor (film)")_'s joint win in the Best Live Action Short category marked the fifth occurrence of a tie in Oscar history; the next tie would occur at the [85th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/85th_Academy_Awards "85th Academy Awards") in 2013.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-16)

## Ceremony information

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Ceremony information")]

Despite earning critical praise for the [previous year's ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards "66th Academy Awards"), actress and comedian [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") announced that she would not host the ceremony for a second consecutive year saying, "I've had a great time, but I've done it."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-22) She added that her role in the upcoming movie _[Bogus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogus\_(film) "Bogus (film)")_ would jeopardize her busy schedule.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-No_Goldberg_or_Crystal-23) In addition, her [Comic Relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_Relief_USA "Comic Relief USA") co-host and veteran Oscar emcee [Billy Crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Crystal "Billy Crystal") declined to host the show citing his commitment to his film _[Forget Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forget\_Paris "Forget Paris")_ which he directed, wrote, starred in, and produced.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-No_Goldberg_or_Crystal-23) Producer Gil Cates hired actor, comedian, and _[Late Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Show\_with\_David\_Letterman "Late Show with David Letterman")_ host [David Letterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Letterman "David Letterman") as host of the 1995 ceremony.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-24) Cates explained his decision to hire the late-night talk show host saying, "He's punctual, he's well groomed, and he knows how to keep an audience awake."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Comedy-25)[ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") entertainment president [Ted Harbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Harbert "Ted Harbert") also approved of the choice stating, "If Dave likes the experience, this could be a great answer for the show, just the way [Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Carson "Johnny Carson") did the show for many years."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-26)

As with previous ceremonies he produced, Cates centered the show on a theme. This year, he christened the show with the theme "Comedy and the Movies" commenting "This year, because of the earthquakes and floods and [Bosnia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia "Bosnia") and [Rwanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwanda "Rwanda"), it was a (terrible) year, and therefore seemed a great year to celebrate what movies can really give us, which is an opportunity to go for two hours in the dark and laugh together. Even with television, it's not a community experience unless you have a very big family. So it's unique to movies and theater, and it's this very human thing."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Comedy-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Comedy_Oscars-27) In tandem with the theme, the ceremony's opening number featured a montage produced by [Chuck Workman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Workman "Chuck Workman") featuring scenes of humorous moments from a variety of both comedic and non-comedic films projected on a large screen on the stage. During that segment, actors [Tim Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Curry "Tim Curry"), [Kathy Najimy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Najimy "Kathy Najimy"), and [Mara Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mara_Wilson "Mara Wilson") performed a modified version of the song "[Make 'Em Laugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Make_'Em_Laugh "Make 'Em Laugh")" from the film _[Singin' in the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singin'\_in\_the\_Rain "Singin' in the Rain")_, using [blue screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chroma_key "Chroma key") technology to make it appear that they were jumping in and out of the montage on the screen.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-28) Several collections of film clips were shown throughout the broadcast highlighting various aspects of comedy such as troupes and dialogue.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-29)

Several other people were also involved with the production of the ceremony. [Bill Conti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Conti "Bill Conti") served as musical director and conductor for the event.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-30) Production designer Roy Christopher designed a new stage for the ceremony which prominently featured a [proscenium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proscenium "Proscenium") which was designed to resemble the iris of a camera.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-31) Moreover, Christopher commented that the iris motif was inspired by the [iris shot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_shot "Iris shot") prominently featured in several comedic films and shorts.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Comedy_Oscars-27) Dancer Debbie Allen choreographed _[The Lion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_King "The Lion King")_ musical number.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-32) Actors [Alec Baldwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alec_Baldwin "Alec Baldwin"), [Jack Lemmon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Lemmon "Jack Lemmon"), [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin"), and [Rosie O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosie_O'Donnell "Rosie O'Donnell") participated in a pre-taped comedic sketch lampooning auditions for a role in _[Cabin Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabin\_Boy "Cabin Boy")_, the film in which Letterman made his film acting debut.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Wiley_1996_982-33)

### Box office performance of nominees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Box office performance of nominees")]

At the time of the nominations announcement on February 14, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees at the US box office was $468 million, with an average of $93.6 million per film.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-BoxOfficeOscars-34)_Forrest Gump_ was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees with $300 million in domestic box office receipts. The film was followed by _Pulp Fiction_ ($76 million), _Four Weddings and a Funeral_ ($52 million), _Quiz Show_ ($21 million) and _The Shawshank Redemption_ ($16 million).[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-BoxOfficeOscars-34)

Of the top 50 grossing movies of the year, 44 nominations went to 14 films on the list. Only _Forrest Gump_ (2nd), _The Client_ (12th), _Pulp Fiction_ (14th), _Four Weddings and a Funeral_ (20th), and _Nell_ (41st) were nominated for directing, acting, screenwriting, or Best Picture. The other top 50 box office hits that earned nominations were _The Lion King_ (1st), _True Lies_ (3rd), _Clear and Present Danger_ (6th), _Speed_ (7th), _The Mask_ (8th), _Interview with the Vampire_ (10th), _Maverick_ (11th), _Legends of the Fall_ (27th) and _Little Women_ (31st).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-35)

### Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

The show received a negative reception from most media publications. John J. O'Connor of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ wrote, "Instead of keeping things moving smartly, Mr. Letterman stuck with his late-night shtick, too often leaving the show's pacing in shambles." He also added, "Within the show's first half-hour, with no strong hand at the helm, the audience simply sagged. Applause died long before most winners even reached the podium."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-36) Television critic John Carman of the _[San Francisco Chronicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Francisco\_Chronicle "San Francisco Chronicle")_ commented, "Last night on ABC, no one got it. Hollywood's big event was wonderfully littered by technical errors, bad taste, low comedy and lower necklines." Moreover, he remarked, "Letterman, the rookie host, was off his game in his opening monologue. Maybe it was the big auditorium. Or a billion people in the television audience."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-37) Film critic [Andrew Sarris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Sarris "Andrew Sarris") of _[The New York Observer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Observer "The New York Observer")_ quipped, "Not only was he not witty or funny, he never knew when to let bad enough alone." He concluded, "As the evening dragged on, it became obvious that Mr. Letterman had no gift for ad-libbing through the few unpredictable opportunities in a 'live' event like the Oscars."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-38)

Some media outlets received the broadcast more positively. Television critic Joyce Millman of _[The San Francisco Examiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_San\_Francisco\_Examiner "The San Francisco Examiner")_ noted, "In his first stint as host of the Oscar telecast, David Letterman did the impossible—he made something entertaining from what is traditionally the most boring three hours of TV this side of a [test pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testcard "Testcard")."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-39)_[The Buffalo News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Buffalo\_News "The Buffalo News")_ columnist Alan Pergament praised Letterman's performance as host writing "David Letterman was a box full of chocolates on an Oscar night that was empty of much emotion until the expected _Forrest Gump_ sweep in the final 15 minutes." He also added that despite a lack of surprises amongst the awards, the emotional and unexpected humorous moments provided depth and entertainment throughout the evening.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-40) Hal Boedeker of the _[Orlando Sentinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando\_Sentinel "Orlando Sentinel")_ gave an average review of the ceremony but singled out Letterman noting that he "proved Monday night that he's among Oscar's Top 10 Hosts. He's definitely at the top of the list with Johnny Carson, Billy Crystal and [Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope "Bob Hope")."[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-41)

### Ratings and reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=67th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Ratings and reception")]

The American telecast on ABC drew an average of 48.28 million people over its length, which was a 7% increase from the [previous year's ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards "66th Academy Awards").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Oscar_ratings-42)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-LA-43) An estimated 81 million total viewers watched all or part of the awards.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-44) The show also drew higher [Nielsen ratings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_ratings "Nielsen ratings") compared to the previous ceremony with 32.5% of households watching over a 53 share.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-LA-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-TVB_Oscars-45) It also drew a higher 18–49 demographic rating with a 21.7 rating among viewers in that demographic.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-TVB_Oscars-45) It was the most watched Oscars telecast since the [55th ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55th_Academy_Awards "55th Academy Awards") held in 1983.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-46)

In July 1995, the ceremony presentation received six nominations at the [47th Primetime Emmys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/47th_Primetime_Emmy_Awards "47th Primetime Emmy Awards").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-47) Two months later, the ceremony won one of those nominations for Jeff Margolis's direction of the telecast.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-48)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-49)

The **66th Academy Awards** ceremony, organized by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") (AMPAS), honored [films released in 1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_in_film "1993 in film") and took place on March 21, 1994, at the [Dorothy Chandler Pavilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Chandler_Pavilion "Dorothy Chandler Pavilion") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") beginning at 6:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 9:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"). During the ceremony, AMPAS presented [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 23 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company"), was produced by [Gil Cates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Cates "Gilbert Cates") and directed by [Jeff Margolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Margolis "Jeff Margolis").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-4) Actor [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") hosted the show for the first time.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-5) Nearly a month earlier in a ceremony held at [The Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California") on February 26, the [Academy Awards for Technical Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Technical_Achievement "Academy Award for Technical Achievement") were presented by host [Laura Dern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Dern "Laura Dern").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-6)

_[Schindler's List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schindler's\_List "Schindler's List")_ won seven awards, including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-7) Other winners included _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(film) "Jurassic Park (film)")_ and _[The Piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Piano "The Piano")_ with three awards, _[Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia\_(film) "Philadelphia (film)")_ with two, and _[The Age of Innocence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Age\_of\_Innocence\_(1993\_film) "The Age of Innocence (1993 film)")_, _[Belle Époque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belle\_%C3%89poque\_(film) "Belle Époque (film)")_, _[Defending Our Lives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defending\_Our\_Lives "Defending Our Lives")_, _[The Fugitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fugitive\_(1993\_film) "The Fugitive (1993 film)")_, _[I Am a Promise: The Children of Stanton Elementary School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Am\_a\_Promise:\_The\_Children\_of\_Stanton\_Elementary\_School "I Am a Promise: The Children of Stanton Elementary School")_, _[Mrs. Doubtfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrs.\_Doubtfire "Mrs. Doubtfire")_, _[Schwarzfahrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schwarzfahrer "Schwarzfahrer")_, and _[The Wrong Trousers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wrong\_Trousers "The Wrong Trousers")_ with one. The telecast was watched by more than 46 million viewers in the United States.

## Winners and nominees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=66th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Winners and nominees")]

The nominees for the 66th Academy Awards were announced on February 9, 1994, at the [Samuel Goldwyn Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Goldwyn_Theater "Samuel Goldwyn Theater") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), by Academy president [Arthur Hiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Hiller "Arthur Hiller") and actress [Christine Lahti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Lahti "Christine Lahti").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-8)_[Schindler's List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schindler's\_List "Schindler's List")_ led all nominees with twelve nominations; _[The Piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Piano "The Piano")_ and _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ tied for second with eight.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-10)

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 21, 1994. Best Director nominee [Jane Campion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Campion "Jane Campion") became the second woman to be nominated in that category.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-11)[Holly Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_Hunter "Holly Hunter") and [Emma Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Thompson "Emma Thompson")'s nominations in both lead and supporting acting categories marked the first, and so far, only occurrence that two performers earned [double acting nominations in the same year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_actors_nominated_for_multiple_Academy_Awards_in_the_same_year "List of actors nominated for multiple Academy Awards in the same year").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-12) Best Supporting Actress winner [Anna Paquin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Paquin "Anna Paquin") became the first [Millennial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennials "Millennials") member to win an Academy Award and, at age 11, the second youngest winner of a competitive acting Oscar, behind [Tatum O'Neal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatum_O'Neal "Tatum O'Neal"), who won at age 10 for _[Paper Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paper\_Moon\_(film) "Paper Moon (film)")_ (1973).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-13)

## Ceremony information

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=66th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Ceremony information")]

[![Image 20: Headshot of Whoopi Goldberg. She has thick black hair and is wearing large hoop earrings.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Whoopi_Goldberg_Cannes_1992.jpg/250px-Whoopi_Goldberg_Cannes_1992.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Whoopi_Goldberg_Cannes_1992.jpg)

[Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") hosted the 66th Academy Awards.

Due to the negative reception received from the [preceding year's ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/65th_Academy_Awards "65th Academy Awards"), actor [Billy Crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Crystal "Billy Crystal") announced that after overseeing four consecutive Oscar ceremonies, he would not be hosting the 1994 telecast.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-20) In a statement released by his publicist, he stated, "After three [Grammys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy "Grammy"), four Oscars and six _[Comic Reliefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic\_Relief "Comic Relief")_, I'm going to take a break from my hosting duties. I always felt honored to host the show and did my best to carry on the tradition of [Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope "Bob Hope") and [Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Carson "Johnny Carson"). I hope the new host has as good a time as I did."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-21) With Crystal absent to host the Oscars, many media outlets wondered whom producer [Gil Cates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gil_Cates "Gil Cates") would hire to emcee the program. Film columnist Jack Matthews suggested that actor [Tom Hanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hanks "Tom Hanks"), who would eventually win Best Actor for _[Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia\_(film) "Philadelphia (film)")_, should host the show writing that he "has charm, dignity, wit, intelligence and, it's worth mentioning, he's a movie star!"[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-HostingRole-22) Cates also offered the role to performers [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin"), [Bette Midler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bette_Midler "Bette Midler"), and [Johnny Carson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Carson "Johnny Carson"), but they all turned down the opportunity.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-HostingRole-22)

After several days of speculation, Cates announced that he hired Oscar-winning actress and comedian [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") to host the festivities for the first time.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-23) By virtue of her selection, Goldberg became both the first [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American "African American") to host as well as the first woman to host the telecast solo.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-24) In an interview with the _Los Angeles Times_, Cates explained the decision to hire her saying, "She is a highly recognizable star who has millions of fans."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-25) He also addressed the media's concerns regarding Goldberg's raunchy and outspoken humor stating, "Some people may think she's potentially dangerous, and she says things that come to her mind. It's going to be exciting for me. The main thing is she wants to do it and she's smart. Whatever she says will be appropriate."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-26) Goldberg expressed that she was thrilled to be selected to emcee the 1994 ceremony commenting, "To go from watching to winning to hosting in one lifetime is major."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-27)

As with previous ceremonies he produced, Cates centered the show around a theme. This year, he christened the show with the theme "People Behind the Camera" commenting that "It will be a salute to those unseen men and women who make what we see on the screen, the artist and craftspeople responsible for the magic of the movies."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-28) In tandem with the theme, the ceremony's opening number featured a montage produced by [Chuck Workman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Workman "Chuck Workman") saluting the many individuals such as directors, editors, and composers who are involved in moviemaking. During that segment, singer [Bernadette Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernadette_Peters "Bernadette Peters") performing a modified version of [Stephen Sondheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Sondheim "Stephen Sondheim")'s song "Putting It Together" from his musical _[Sunday in the Park with George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday\_in\_the\_Park\_with\_George "Sunday in the Park with George")_.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-29) Filmmaker and editor Carol A. Streit assembled another montage featuring a salute to the work of cinematographers and their contributions to film.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-30)

Several other people and elements were also involved with the production of the ceremony. Production designer Roy Christopher designed a new stage for the ceremony which prominently featured five giant Oscar statues each flanked inside metal cones that were illuminated recurrently throughout the show.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Oscar_Time-31) Film composer and musician [Bill Conti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Conti "Bill Conti") served as musical director of the ceremony.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-32) Dancer [Debbie Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Allen "Debbie Allen") choreographed a dancer number showcasing the Best Original Score nominees featuring eight prestigious ballet and dance troupes from around the world.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-BalletDance-19)

An [in memoriam segment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_memoriam_segment "In memoriam segment") was introduced for the first time during the ceremony. In subsequent years, it became the permanent element of the Oscars.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-33)

### Box office performance of nominees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=66th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Box office performance of nominees")]

At the time of the nominations announcement on February 9, the combined gross of the five Best Picture nominees at the US box office was $261 million, with an average of $52.2 million per film.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-BoxOfficeOscars-34)_The Fugitive_ was the highest earner among the Best Picture nominees with $179 million in domestic box office receipts.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-BoxOfficeOscars-34) The film was followed by _Schindler's List_ ($29.6 million), _The Piano_ ($25.7 million), _The Remains of the Day_ ($19.5 million), and finally _In the Name of the Father_ ($6.5 million).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-BoxOfficeOscars-34)

Of the top 50 grossing movies of the year, 36 nominations went to 14 films on the list. Only _The Fugitive_ (3rd), _The Firm_ (4th), _Sleepless in Seattle_ (6th), _In the Line of Fire_ (7th), _Dave_ (13th), _Philadelphia_ (29th), _What's Love Got to Do With It_ (38th), and _The Age of Innocence_ (49th) were nominated for directing, acting, screenwriting, or Best Picture.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-boxofficemojooscars-35) The other top 50 box office hits that earned nominations were _Jurassic Park_ (1st), _Mrs. Doubtfire_ (2nd), _Cliffhanger_ (9th), _The Nightmare Before Christmas_ (24th), _Addams Family Values_ (25th), and _Beethoven's 2nd_ (27th).[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-boxofficemojooscars-35)

### Critical reviews

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=66th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Critical reviews")]

The show received a positive reception from most media publications. _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ film critic [Janet Maslin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janet_Maslin "Janet Maslin") raved that the telecast had "less silliness and less small talk, with more emphasis on cleverly chosen film clips and the bona fide Hollywood magic being celebrated." She also praised host Goldberg saying that she "sustained a tone of levity, which became particularly important as the sweep by _Schindler's List_ threatened to bring out great ponderousness in some quarters."[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-36)_[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh\_Post-Gazette "Pittsburgh Post-Gazette")_ television critic Robert Bianco commended Goldberg's performance writing that "She never acted like she was too smart or to hip for the show she was hosting; she never smirked like there was a joke she alone was cool enough to get." He also extolled producer Cates by commenting, "In place of the extraneous jokes and terrible production numbers, he gave us a theme that worked and a generous selection of clips to back it up."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-37)[Anne Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anne_Thompson_(film_critic) "Anne Thompson (film critic)") of _[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment\_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")_ lauded Goldberg by stating, "Her elegant appearance (at least during the first half), her uncharacteristic restraint (she didn't cuss), and her ability to make it funny (despite the very somber speeches) made the ho-hum telecast worth watching."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-38)

Some media outlets were more critical of the show. Television critic [Howard Rosenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Rosenberg "Howard Rosenberg") of the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ lamented that Goldberg's humor "wilted in a blessedly brief 3-hour-and-18-minute telecast." He also wrote that compared with Billy Crystal, her hosting skills were "balmy".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-39)_[Orlando Sentinel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando\_Sentinel "Orlando Sentinel")_ film critic Jay Boyar bemoaned that "this year's Oscarcast was only a little more exciting than a wine snob droning on about his favorite vintages."[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-40) Harold Schindler of _[The Salt Lake City Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Salt\_Lake\_City\_Tribune "The Salt Lake City Tribune")_ remarked that Whoopi's preference for "insider" jokes "left the audience murmuring and most viewers probably scratching their heads." He also added the biggest letdown of the telecast was "Goldberg's seeming ineptness at understanding the moment"[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-41)

### Ratings and reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=66th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Ratings and reception")]

The American telecast on ABC drew in an average of 46.26 million people over its length, which was a 1% increase from the [previous year's ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/65th_Academy_Awards "65th Academy Awards").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-43) However, the show drew lower [Nielsen ratings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_ratings "Nielsen ratings") compared to the previous ceremony with 31.86% of households watching over a 49.28 share.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-TVB_Oscars-44) It also drew a lower 18–49 demographic rating with a 19.73 rating over a 40.53 share among viewers in that demographic.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-TVB_Oscars-44)

In July 1994, the ceremony presentation received seven nominations at the [46th Primetime Emmys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/46th_Primetime_Emmy_Awards "46th Primetime Emmy Awards").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-46) Two months later, the ceremony won one of those nominations for Outstanding Technical Direction/Camera/Video for a Miniseries or Special (Averill Perry, Jim Ralston, Kenneth R. Shapiro, Bill Pope, Hector Ramirez, Larry Heider, Dave Levisohn, Blair White, Bill Philben, Ralph Alcocer, Larry Stenman, Bud Holland, David Irete, Tom Geren, Dale Carlson, David Plakos, Ted Ashton, Jeff Mydoc, Chuck Pharis, Jean M. Mason).[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-47)

The **66th Academy Awards** ceremony, organized by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") (AMPAS), honored [films released in 1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_in_film "1993 in film") and took place on March 21, 1994, at the [Dorothy Chandler Pavilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Chandler_Pavilion "Dorothy Chandler Pavilion") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") beginning at 6:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 9:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"). During the ceremony, AMPAS presented [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 23 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company"), was produced by [Gil Cates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Cates "Gilbert Cates") and directed by [Jeff Margolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Margolis "Jeff Margolis").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-4) Actor [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") hosted the show for the first time.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-5) Nearly a month earlier in a ceremony held at [The Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California") on February 26, the [Academy Awards for Technical Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Technical_Achievement "Academy Award for Technical Achievement") were presented by host [Laura Dern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Dern "Laura Dern").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-6)

_[Schindler's List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schindler's\_List "Schindler's List")_ won seven awards, including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-7) Other winners included _[Jurassic Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jurassic\_Park\_(film) "Jurassic Park (film)")_ and _[The Piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Piano "The Piano")_ with three awards, _[Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia\_(film) "Philadelphia (film)")_ with two, and _[The Age of Innocence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Age\_of\_Innocence\_(1993\_film) "The Age of Innocence (1993 film)")_, _[Belle Époque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belle\_%C3%89poque\_(film) "Belle Époque (film)")_, _[Defending Our Lives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defending\_Our\_Lives "Defending Our Lives")_, _[The Fugitive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fugitive\_(1993\_film) "The Fugitive (1993 film)")_, _[I Am a Promise: The Children of Stanton Elementary School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Am\_a\_Promise:\_The\_Children\_of\_Stanton\_Elementary\_School "I Am a Promise: The Children of Stanton Elementary School")_, _[Mrs. Doubtfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mrs.\_Doubtfire "Mrs. Doubtfire")_, _[Schwarzfahrer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schwarzfahrer "Schwarzfahrer")_, and _[The Wrong Trousers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wrong\_Trousers "The Wrong Trousers")_ with one. The telecast was watched by more than 46 million viewers in the United States.

## Winners and nominees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=66th_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Winners and nominees")]

The nominees for the 66th Academy Awards were announced on February 9, 1994, at the [Samuel Goldwyn Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Goldwyn_Theater "Samuel Goldwyn Theater") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), by Academy president [Arthur Hiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Hiller "Arthur Hiller") and actress [Christine Lahti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Lahti "Christine Lahti").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-8)_[Schindler's List](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schindler's\_List "Schindler's List")_ led all nominees with twelve nominations; _[The Piano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Piano "The Piano")_ and _[The Remains of the Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Remains\_of\_the\_Day\_(film) "The Remains of the Day (film)")_ tied for second with eight.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-10)

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on March 21, 1994. Best Director nominee [Jane Campion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Campion "Jane Campion") became the second woman to be nominated in that category.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-11)[Holly Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_Hunter "Holly Hunter") and [Emma Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emma_Thompson "Emma Thompson")'s nominations in both lead and supporting acting categories marked the first, and so far, only occurrence that two performers earned [double acting nominations in the same year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_actors_nominated_for_multiple_Academy_Awards_in_the_same_year "List of actors nominated for multiple Academy Awards in the same year").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-12) Best Supporting Actress winner [Anna Paquin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Paquin "Anna Paquin") became the first [Millennial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennials "Millennials") member to win an Academy Award and, at age 11, the second youngest winner of a competitive acting Oscar, behind [Tatum O'Neal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatum_O'Neal "Tatum O'Neal"), who won at age 10 for _[Paper Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paper\_Moon\_(film) "Paper Moon (film)")_ (1973).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Academy_Awards#cite_note-13)
